name: Plywood & Wood Boards
tagline: The carcass behind every wardrobe, kitchen and storage unit
description: Boards are the first specification decision on any interior job: they set the cost, the lifespan and how the joinery behaves in a damp Indian summer. This section covers plywood by bonding grade, engineered boards like MDF and HDHMR, and the plastic-based boards that have taken over wet areas.

materials.name: MR plywood
materials.blurb: Moisture-resistant interior grade — the default for dry-area joinery
materials.description: Bonded with urea-formaldehyde resin, MR ply handles humidity but not standing water. It is the workhorse board for wardrobes, beds and TV units in dry rooms, and the cheapest plywood worth specifying on a paying job.

materials.name: BWR plywood
materials.blurb: Boiling-water-resistant grade for kitchens and utility joinery
materials.description: BWR uses phenolic resin, so it survives repeated wetting and drying far better than MR. Specify it wherever splashes are routine but full immersion is not — kitchen carcasses, utility storage and washbasin counters.

materials.name: BWP / Marine plywood
materials.blurb: Fully waterproof marine grade for wet areas and outdoor joinery
materials.description: The top bonding grade in the IS system, tested against 72 hours of boiling water. Worth the premium for sink units, bathroom vanities, balcony joinery and anything that will sit against an external wall.

materials.name: Commercial plywood
materials.blurb: Budget MR-grade board for backing panels and low-load work
materials.description: Lighter core, thinner face veneers and a lower price. Fine for back panels, shutters that carry no load and site-level temporary work — not for anything that must hold a hinge for a decade.

materials.name: Fire-retardant plywood
materials.blurb: Chemically treated board for escape routes and public interiors
materials.description: Impregnated with fire-retardant chemicals so flame spread is slowed and the board self-extinguishes. Commonly mandated in hotels, offices, hospitals and any interior work near an escape corridor.

materials.name: Flexible plywood
materials.blurb: Bends to a curve without steaming — for columns and curved fronts
materials.description: Cross-grain construction lets the sheet roll in one direction. Two layers laminated over a former give a stable curved panel for reception desks, curved bedbacks and column cladding.

materials.name: Shuttering plywood
materials.blurb: Film-faced board for concrete formwork, reusable many times
materials.description: A phenolic film face lets concrete release cleanly and survives repeated pours. On interior sites it also turns up as a rugged working surface and protection board during the messy trades.

materials.name: Blockboard
materials.blurb: Softwood-batten core — light and straight over long spans
materials.description: Strips of softwood sandwiched between veneers make a board that stays flat across a long shutter and weighs much less than ply. The classic choice for tall wardrobe shutters, door panels and long shelves.

materials.name: Calibrated plywood
materials.blurb: Sanded to an exact thickness — the base for veneer and laminate
materials.description: Machine-sanded to a tight thickness tolerance so pressed veneer or laminate lies perfectly flat with no telegraphing. Specify it whenever a high-gloss or veneered face has to look faultless.

materials.name: MDF
materials.blurb: Dense, uniform fibreboard — the surface for paint and routing
materials.description: No grain, no voids and a face smooth enough to spray directly. Ideal for CNC-routed panels, painted shutters and mouldings, but it swells badly if water reaches an unsealed edge.

materials.name: HDHMR
materials.blurb: High-density, high-moisture-resistant board — screws like ply, finishes like MDF
materials.description: A denser cousin of MDF made to hold fasteners and resist swelling. It has become the default modular-kitchen board where a laminate finish and good screw-holding both matter.

materials.name: HDF
materials.blurb: Very dense thin board for laminate flooring cores and back panels
materials.description: Denser and harder than MDF, usually seen as the core of laminate flooring or as a rigid thin back panel. Excellent surface hardness, poor tolerance of standing water.

materials.name: Particle board
materials.blurb: Lowest-cost engineered board for flat-pack and low-load furniture
materials.description: Wood chips bonded under pressure — cheap, flat and stable in dry conditions. Best kept to flat-pack furniture, office workstations and anywhere the budget will not stretch to HDHMR.

materials.name: Pre-laminated MDF
materials.blurb: MDF with the decorative face already pressed on — no site lamination
materials.description: Comes out of the factory finished on both faces, so carpentry is cut-and-assemble only. Saves days on fast-track jobs; the trade-off is a fixed palette and edges that must be banded.

materials.name: Pre-laminated particle board
materials.blurb: Factory-finished particle board for high-volume, low-cost furniture
materials.description: The cheapest finished board on the market and the backbone of budget office furniture. Specify with sealed edges and keep it well away from wet areas.

materials.name: WPC board
materials.blurb: Wood-plastic composite — termite-proof and genuinely waterproof
materials.description: A PVC-and-wood-flour composite that does not swell, rot or feed termites. It has largely replaced marine ply in bathroom vanities and balcony joinery, though it is softer and holds screws less firmly.

materials.name: PVC foam board
materials.blurb: Lightweight rigid foam sheet for wet zones and signage
materials.description: All plastic, zero moisture absorption, very light to handle. Good for bathroom shutters, service-duct covers and signage; not suitable where hinges and handles will see heavy daily load.

materials.name: OSB
materials.blurb: Oriented strand board — structural sheathing with a graphic face
materials.description: Large wood strands bonded in oriented layers make a strong, cheap structural sheet. In interiors it is used as an exposed finish in cafés, studios and industrial-look retail.

materials.name: Bamboo board
materials.blurb: Fast-renewable hardwood alternative with a distinctive linear grain
materials.description: Compressed bamboo strips give a board harder than most hardwoods, with a fine linear figure that finishes beautifully in oil. A strong sustainability story for worktops, shelving and table tops.
